name: Pastel Green
lede: Pastel green is a soft, light green, named for its pale chalky look rather than for any one dye or pigment.

sections.title: A soft green
sections.body:
The books use *pastel green* as a loose description, not a defined color. Paterson uses it to define two other names: celadon, a name used in glazing Chinese porcelain, and mint green, the green of mint leaves [1][2]. [[celadon]] is a green with a history, which pastel green lacks [1].

In writing it signals the mild and the fashionable. Greenfield sets it beside acid pink as the kind of trend a cautious dresser avoids when choosing black [3]. Finlay uses it for the soft green of eucalyptus clumps in the pink Australian desert where opal is mined [4]. In both cases it means a gentle green set against something stronger [3][4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of museum paintings, a color near this swatch is present in only 9 works, 0.04 per cent of the archive [5]. The earliest is a work of 1488 and the latest dates from 1924 [5]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, so read the numbers as screen colors [5].
